projects.name: Aurem
projects.description: Online class excludes whoever cannot hear.
highlights: Redux over Context — the classroom has state shared by three roles; in Context that becomes cascading re-renders on every transcribed sentence.
Fabric.js on the whiteboard — annotation had to travel as vector, not image: it syncs as data and stays sharp at any zoom.
WebSockets over polling — the latency budget ran from speech to text on screen; polling blew it on the round-trip alone.
Electron frameless with click-through — the caption must sit on top of PowerPoint without stealing the presenter's click.
Web Speech API — client-side transcription cut one server round-trip per sentence and kept audio off the wire.
projects.x_detail: Live captioning with the Web Speech API, a collaborative whiteboard in Fabric.js, and an Electron client whose transparent overlay captions on top of any software.

projects.name: Maincore
projects.description: Institutional site that has to sell two technical product lines and capture qualified leads.
highlights: styled-components with ServerStyleSheet — CSS ships inside the server HTML. Without it the first paint arrives unstyled, and this page is the company's first commercial contact.
Radix for accordion and menu — product specs live in accordions. Keyboard, focus and ARIA out of the box cost less than reimplementing them wrong.
reCAPTCHA verified server-side — the token only counts once the backend confirms it with Google. Client-side validation is decorative.
Own SMTP instead of a form service — the lead lands straight in the company mailbox, with no third party holding customer data.
One route per product — Polaris and Sirius on separate URLs instead of tabs. A product that must rank needs its own address.
projects.x_detail: Next.js 13 with styled-components on the server, Radix for the interactive components, and lead capture with the captcha verified in the backend.

projects.name: This portfolio
projects.description: Developer portfolios assert competence. This one tries to prove it.
highlights: Sentry in Terraform, not the dashboard — production alerting is infrastructure. In code it goes through PR and keeps history; a Go contract test validates the rule before apply.
Gitleaks over full history — public repo that deploys infra. A secret leaked in an old commit is still leaked; scanning only the diff does not help.
Actions pinned to SHAs — tags are mutable, SHAs are not. Dependabot proposes the bump, I review it.
Terraform plan never posted on PRs — the check status is public, the plan is not. Plans expose production topology in open pull requests.
Serialized apply in a protected environment — runs only on protected master, after every check, inside a GitHub production environment.
axe-playwright in CI — accessibility that does not run in the pipeline rots on the first tight sprint.
Consent before any event — no analytics fires before the choice.
projects.x_detail: Feature-based architecture with MVVM, unit, e2e and a11y tests running in CI, i18n, consent and Sentry. It ships through GitHub Actions with Terraform.
